headline: What the new North Sea allocation actually changes for a boat under twelve metres
standfirst: The headline figure went up. For most of the small-boat fleet, the number that matters went down.

image.alt: A small inshore fishing boat alongside a stone quay

body.text: The total allowable catch rose by six per cent. That is the number in the press release, and it is accurate. It is also close to meaningless if you fish a ten-metre boat out of a harbour that dries at low water.

Allocation is done by track record. Track record is calculated from historic landings. Boats that were tied up during the reference years — which includes most of the under-twelve fleet during the fuel crisis — carry a smaller share into every subsequent round.

items: Under-ten-metre pool: down 2% in real terms
Quota leasing cost: up roughly 30% year on year

body.text: The under-ten pool is topped up by ministerial discretion each year, which makes it impossible to plan against. Two of the three producer organisations have asked for a fixed percentage instead. Neither has received an answer.
